headline.purpose: Page-level h1s: Bookings, Teams, onboarding step titles.

card-title.purpose: Card headings; labels a region rather than opening one. Drops to 14px in a data-size=sm card.

body.purpose: Default UI text: table cells, form labels, descriptions. Caps prose at 65-75ch. Inputs render 16px below md to defeat iOS focus zoom.

shadows.name: floating-menu

shadows.name: floating-panel

shadows.name: ring-as-shadow
shadows.purpose: Outline sidebar-menu-button hairline drawn as a shadow so it never affects layout. Shifts to --sidebar-accent on hover.

shadows.name: chrome-lift
shadows.purpose: Floating and inset sidebar variants only - detached shell chrome, never content.

shadows.name: none
shadows.purpose: Cards, dialogs, and every in-page surface. Separation is ring-1 ring-foreground/10 plus a one-notch tonal shift.

components.name: Primary Button
components.description: The workhorse action. Solid charcoal; used for the default commit on any surface.
components.css: .ds-btn { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; gap: 0.375rem; height: 2rem; padding: 0 0.625rem; border: 1px solid transparent; border-radius: var(--radius, 0.25rem); font-family: var(--font-jakarta), 'Plus Jakarta Sans', system-ui, sans-serif; font-size: 0.875rem; font-weight: 500; white-space: nowrap; cursor: pointer; transition: all 200ms; outline: none; } .ds-btn:focus-visible { border-color: var(--ring); box-shadow: 0 0 0 3px color-mix(in oklab, var(--ring) 50%, transparent); } .ds-btn:active { transform: translateY(1px); } .ds-btn:disabled { opacity: 0.5; cursor: not-allowed; } .ds-btn-primary { background: var(--primary); color: var(--primary-foreground); }

components.name: Brand Button
components.description: The single most important action on a surface. The only place the teal appears as a solid fill.
components.css: .ds-btn-brand { background: var(--brand); color: var(--brand-foreground); } .ds-btn-brand:hover { background: color-mix(in oklab, var(--brand) 90%, transparent); } .ds-btn-brand:focus-visible { border-color: color-mix(in oklab, var(--brand) 40%, transparent); box-shadow: 0 0 0 3px color-mix(in oklab, var(--brand) 50%, transparent); }

components.name: Outline Button
components.description: Secondary action. Page-colored fill with a hairline stroke; hovers to the muted tone.
components.css: .ds-btn-outline { background: var(--background); color: var(--foreground); border-color: var(--border); } .ds-btn-outline:hover { background: var(--muted); }

components.name: Destructive Button
components.description: A tinted well, not a solid block - destructive intent is signalled by hue, not by mass, so it never outweighs the primary action beside it.
components.css: .ds-btn-destructive { background: color-mix(in oklab, var(--destructive) 10%, transparent); color: var(--destructive); } .ds-btn-destructive:hover { background: color-mix(in oklab, var(--destructive) 20%, transparent); } .ds-btn-destructive:focus-visible { border-color: color-mix(in oklab, var(--destructive) 40%, transparent); box-shadow: 0 0 0 3px color-mix(in oklab, var(--destructive) 20%, transparent); }

components.name: Text Input
components.description: 2rem tall, transparent fill, hairline stroke. Focus pulls in the brand teal so the accent reinforces itself.
components.css: .ds-input { height: 2rem; width: 100%; padding: 0.25rem 0.625rem; background: transparent; color: var(--foreground); border: 1px solid var(--input); border-radius: var(--radius, 0.25rem); font-family: var(--font-jakarta), 'Plus Jakarta Sans', system-ui, sans-serif; font-size: 0.875rem; transition: border-color 200ms, box-shadow 200ms; outline: none; } .ds-input::placeholder { color: var(--muted-foreground); } .ds-input:focus-visible { border-color: var(--ring); box-shadow: 0 0 0 3px color-mix(in oklab, var(--ring) 50%, transparent); } .ds-input[aria-invalid='true'] { border-color: var(--destructive); box-shadow: 0 0 0 3px color-mix(in oklab, var(--destructive) 20%, transparent); } .ds-input:disabled { opacity: 0.5; cursor: not-allowed; }

components.name: Card
components.description: Flat by definition. A hairline ring plus a one-notch lightness shift does the work a shadow would do elsewhere. Sharp-cornered at the default radius preset.
components.html:
Upcoming sessions
Next 7 days
3 bookings, 1 inquiry awaiting reply.
components.css: .ds-card { display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: 1rem; padding: 1rem 0; overflow: hidden; background: var(--card); color: var(--card-foreground); border-radius: var(--radius-surface, 0rem); box-shadow: inset 0 0 0 1px color-mix(in oklab, var(--foreground) 10%, transparent); font-family: var(--font-jakarta), 'Plus Jakarta Sans', system-ui, sans-serif; font-size: 0.875rem; } .ds-card-header { display: grid; gap: 0.25rem; padding: 0 1rem; } .ds-card-title { font-size: 1rem; font-weight: 500; line-height: 1.375; } .ds-card-desc { font-size: 0.875rem; color: var(--muted-foreground); } .ds-card-content { padding: 0 1rem; }

components.name: Status Badge
components.description: 1.25rem status chip. Shares the button variant vocabulary so a badge and a button describing the same state agree in color. Static badges carry no hover.
components.css: .ds-badge { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; gap: 0.25rem; height: 1.25rem; padding: 0.125rem 0.5rem; border: 1px solid transparent; border-radius: calc(var(--radius, 0.25rem) * 0.8); font-family: var(--font-jakarta), 'Plus Jakarta Sans', system-ui, sans-serif; font-size: 0.75rem; font-weight: 500; white-space: nowrap; } .ds-badge-booked { background: color-mix(in oklab, var(--event-booked) 14%, transparent); color: var(--event-booked); }

components.name: Sidebar Nav Item
components.description: Active state is a 12% teal wash with teal text and a weight shift - quiet enough for a list of ten, and never signalled by color alone.
components.html: CalendarBookings
components.css: .ds-nav { display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: 0.125rem; width: 16rem; padding: 0.5rem; background: var(--sidebar); border-radius: var(--radius-surface, 0rem); } .ds-nav-item { display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 0.5rem; height: 2rem; padding: 0.5rem; border-radius: calc(var(--radius, 0.25rem) * 0.8); color: var(--sidebar-foreground); font-family: var(--font-jakarta), 'Plus Jakarta Sans', system-ui, sans-serif; font-size: 0.875rem; text-decoration: none; transition: background 200ms, color 200ms; } .ds-nav-item svg { width: 1rem; height: 1rem; flex-shrink: 0; } .ds-nav-item:hover { background: var(--sidebar-accent); color: var(--sidebar-accent-foreground); } .ds-nav-item:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--sidebar-ring); outline-offset: 1px; } .ds-nav-item-active { background: color-mix(in oklab, var(--brand) 12%, transparent); color: var(--brand); font-weight: 500; }

components.name: Dialog
components.description: Flat like a card - the backdrop already detaches it, so it takes a hairline ring and no shadow. Sharp frame, soft controls inside it.
components.html:
Cancel this booking?
The client will be notified. This cannot be undone.
components.css: .ds-dialog { display: grid; gap: 1rem; max-width: 24rem; padding: 1rem; background: var(--popover); color: var(--popover-foreground); border-radius: var(--radius-surface, 0rem); box-shadow: inset 0 0 0 1px color-mix(in oklab, var(--foreground) 10%, transparent); font-family: var(--font-jakarta), 'Plus Jakarta Sans', system-ui, sans-serif; font-size: 0.875rem; } .ds-dialog-title { font-size: 1.25rem; font-weight: 600; line-height: 1.3; letter-spacing: -0.01em; } .ds-dialog-body { color: var(--muted-foreground); } .ds-dialog-actions { display: flex; justify-content: flex-end; gap: 0.5rem; }

components.name: Dropdown Menu
components.description: A floating overlay, so it earns a shadow plus the hairline ring - the one case where shadow is correct in this system.
components.html:
Edit booking
Duplicate
Delete
components.css: .ds-menu { min-width: 12rem; padding: 0.25rem; background: var(--popover); color: var(--popover-foreground); border-radius: var(--radius, 0.25rem); box-shadow: 0 4px 6px -1px rgb(0 0 0 / 0.1), 0 2px 4px -2px rgb(0 0 0 / 0.1), inset 0 0 0 1px color-mix(in oklab, var(--foreground) 10%, transparent); font-family: var(--font-jakarta), 'Plus Jakarta Sans', system-ui, sans-serif; font-size: 0.875rem; } .ds-menu-item { padding: 0.375rem 0.5rem; border-radius: calc(var(--radius, 0.25rem) * 0.8); cursor: pointer; transition: background 200ms; } .ds-menu-item:hover { background: var(--muted); } .ds-menu-sep { height: 1px; margin: 0.25rem 0; background: var(--border); } .ds-menu-item-danger { color: var(--destructive); } .ds-menu-item-danger:hover { background: color-mix(in oklab, var(--destructive) 10%, transparent); }

narrative.overview:
Gallurio sits where creative work meets exact bookkeeping. An event business's calendar is full of shoots, weddings, and launches - messy, human, deadline-driven - but the tool that runs the business underneath has to be as precise as a ledger: every booking accounted for, every client record trustworthy, nothing left ambiguous. The interface reflects that split. It is quiet and neutral-cool at rest (an almost-white "dirty white" ground, never stark black/white), so the work itself - photos, client names, dates - carries the visual weight. One deliberate accent, a deep teal, marks what's actionable: primary buttons, the active nav item, today's date, a booked event. Everything else stays disciplined and gets out of the way.

The system runs at high density. The default control height is 32px, body copy is 14px, and card padding is 16px - a working instrument, not a showcase. Surfaces are flat and structural frames are sharp-cornered; depth in the resting UI comes from a one-notch tonal shift plus a hairline ring, never a shadow. Shadows exist, but only on things that genuinely float above the page and need to read as detached from it.

This system explicitly rejects the generic SaaS-cream dashboard look (gradient hero-metric tiles, glassmorphism, warm sand/parchment backgrounds, identical icon-card grids), sterile enterprise/legacy-ERP chrome, and visual clutter - competing badges and accents fighting for attention on one screen.
keyCharacteristics: Neutral-cool "dirty white" / soft-charcoal base - never pure black or pure white.
One brand accent (teal, hue 195) used sparingly and consistently for anything actionable.
Flat resting surfaces: a ring-1 ring-foreground/10 hairline does the job shadows would elsewhere. Only floating overlays carry a shadow.
Controls are gently rounded; structural frames (cards, dialogs, sidebar) are sharp-cornered by default, and both are user-switchable through three radius presets.
A theme-invariant event-status vocabulary (booked/completed/cancelled/inquiry) that reads identically in light and dark mode.
Single type family, Plus Jakarta Sans, carrying the whole app hierarchy through weight and size, not font-pairing.
Every token has a tuned dark-mode counterpart; the two schemes share a faint cool hue so they read as one product.

rules.name: The One Accent Rule
rules.body: Teal is the only color allowed to mean "act on this." It never appears decoratively - only on buttons, active states, focus rings, the lead chart series, and the booked-event vocabulary.

rules.name: The Never-Pure Rule
rules.body: Backgrounds and text never hit true #000/#fff. Every neutral carries a faint cool tint (hue ~235 light, ~255 dark) so light and dark mode feel like the same product. This rule governs the app shell; the shipped portfolio presets carry their own version of it.

rules.name: The Theme-Invariant Status Rule
rules.body: Event colors and --off-range hold the same value in both schemes. A calendar must not change its status vocabulary when a user flips the theme.

rules.name: The One Voice Rule
rules.body: No second type family in the application shell. Hierarchy is built from size, weight, and tracking on a single face. The shipped portfolio presets are governed separately.

rules.name: The Flat-Content Rule
rules.body: If it is part of the page, it is flat: hairline ring plus tonal shift. If it floats over the page and could land on anything, it gets a shadow. There is no third case, and no shadow ever appears on a card.

rules.name: The Hairline Rule
rules.body: ring-1 ring-foreground/10 is the standard separator for a raised surface. It is a ring, not a border, so it never participates in layout or shifts content by a pixel.

rules.name: The Two-Axis Rule
rules.body: Never hardcode a corner. A control reads --radius (or its derived step); a frame reads --radius-surface. A literal rounded-md on a card breaks the sharp preset silently.

rules.name: The Preset Quality Bar
rules.body: A shipped portfolio preset is a finished design, not a swatch set. Foreground-on-background clears 4.5:1; the accent clears 4.5:1 against its own ground; and if the button style is solid, the label color clears 4.5:1 against the accent. An accent that only works as an outline button ships only with buttonStyle: outline.

rules.name: The Preset Distinction Rule
rules.body: Each preset must be identifiable at a glance from its ground, accent, and type pairing together. Two presets sharing an accent value is a defect, not a coincidence.

rules.name: The Owner's Page Rule
rules.body: Presets are Gallurio's design; everything the owner does afterwards is not. Do not add validation, nudges, or corrections that push a tenant's chosen colors back toward this system. The public page is the owner's to get wrong.

dos: Do reach for a semantic token (bg-card, text-muted-foreground, ring-border) rather than a literal color. Both schemes, both radius axes, and all future theming flow through them.
Do use --radius on controls and --radius-surface on frames, so a change of corner preset moves the whole UI coherently.
Do separate a raised surface with ring-1 ring-foreground/10 and a tonal step.
Do reserve the brand teal for action and active state: brand buttons, the active nav item, focus rings, today's date, booked events, and the lead chart series.
Do pair every color signal with a second cue - an icon, a label, a weight shift - so state survives both color-blindness and grayscale.
Do ship a prefers-reduced-motion counterpart with every keyframe animation.
Do use logical direction utilities (ms/me, ps/pe, start/end) everywhere, and verify Arabic geometry rather than assuming it.
Do build all four async states (loading, empty, error, populated) and all five control states (idle, hover, focus-visible, active, disabled) for every surface.
Do hold 14px body and 2rem controls as the default density. If a screen needs more room, cut content, not scale.
donts: Don't put a box-shadow on a card, a dialog, or any in-page surface. Shadows belong to floating overlays only.
Don't use pure #000 or #fff for a background or for text in the app shell.
Don't introduce a second type family into the application. Hierarchy comes from size, weight, and tracking on Plus Jakarta Sans.
Don't hardcode a corner radius, a control height, or a hex value; all three are user-switchable axes in disguise.
Don't spend the teal on decoration - a colored heading, a tinted background band, an icon with no action behind it. Past roughly 20% of a view it stops meaning "act on this."
Don't change an event-status color between light and dark mode. That vocabulary is theme-invariant by design.
Don't use physical direction utilities (ml/mr, pl/pr, text-left, left-0) in any component that renders under Arabic.
Don't signal a state with color alone, and don't let a status chip carry hover styling unless it is genuinely a link.
Don't ship a portfolio preset that fails the contrast bar, duplicates another preset's accent, or defaults to the rounded radius.
